messages.subject: A quick question about the alelles.
parts:
Hi Karl,
I queried variants from a dataset using a function generated by "create_variant_query_func". Could you please help me figure out the ref allele and the alt allele in the "alleles" column from the output data frame? I guess it denotes "alt | ref". If it is correct, the genotype of rs265104288 (the first line of the df below) for A_J is GA GA.
Please correct me.
Thanks!
Dan


#generate the func
query_variants <- create_variant_query_func("*/cc_variants.sqlite")

#query snpinfo (all)
snpinfo<-query_variants(chr, 0, 10000000)

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: A quick question about the alelles.
parts:
The script to create that file is at the following: https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/inst/scripts/create_ccvariants.R
The main thing I did was force each to be biallelic as the most common allele vs all others. 

But if there’s a question, it’s always best to go back to the original data from Sanger to double-check; URLs are at the top of that R script.

I think the allele to the left of the vertical bar is the 1 and the one to the right is the 2, so for rs265104288, I’d think A/J was G/G while C57BL6/J was GA/GA.

karl
